overview: Rise 6.0's Disabler is a toggle registry built on the client's module component system. The class itself contains no packet logic: each BooleanValue binds a named bypass to a component class in the exploit/disabler package (CubeCraftDisabler, VulcanDisabler, KeepAliveDisabler and friends), and those components register their own packet listeners against Rise's PACKET_ROUTER. Active toggles target CubeCraft, Mine Land, Verus, Vulcan, UniversoCraft and other anticheats, plus generic primitives: keepalive cancellation, transaction cancellation, sprint entity-action cancellation, spectate injection and forced server teleports. The constructor implements a deprecation system: every setting declared after the Deprecated toggle is hidden from the UI unless that toggle is enabled.

sections.p: The module is a thin composition root. Each bypass lives in its own class under com.alan.clients.module.impl.exploit.disabler, and the Disabler core only wires values to component instances through the BooleanValue constructor. The component pattern is Rise 6.x's standard module organization: a module declares values and components, and the client instantiates and drives both. All packet work is delegated, so the core file stays at 87 lines while the behavior is spread across 19 component classes.

Rise 6.x does not use the vanilla packet event bus that older clients (Gugustus, Tenacity 5.1) expose. Packets are wrapped in the client's own Packet abstraction and routed through PACKET_ROUTER to EventLink/Listener handlers registered by components. The disabler package confirms the shift: movement components hook C03PacketPlayer and its subclasses (C04PacketPlayerPosition, C06PacketPlayerPosLook), while dedicated components eat C00PacketKeepAlive, C0FPacketConfirmTransaction, C0BPacketEntityAction, C07PacketPlayerDigging and C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement. Serverbound spoofs cover C13PacketPlayerAbilities, C17PacketCustomPayload and C18PacketSpectate, and UniversoCraft's state machine watches S07PacketRespawn and C02PacketUseEntity.

The constructor walks getValues() in declaration order with a one-value lookahead. Once it reaches the value whose name equals 'deprecated', every later value gets hideIf = () -> !this.deprecated.getValue(), so the legacy toggles disappear from the UI unless the Deprecated master switch is on. The deprecated block reuses live components: Hypixel Slime binds the same AbilitiesDisabler as Abilities, MMC Partial Reach binds the same TransactionDisabler as Cancel Transactions, and MMC Keep Sprint binds the same SprintDisabler as Cancel Sprint Packet, so those rows are historical UI aliases, not separate implementations.

annotations.text: Package declaration: the module lives in the exploit package of Rise's module tree, grouped with the other anticheat-facing utilities.

Client-framework imports: the @Rise marker annotation, the Module base class, Category and ModuleInfo from the module API, the wildcard import of every Disabler component in the exploit.disabler subpackage, and the Value/BooleanValue settings framework. The wildcard matters: this file never names a component class explicitly beyond the constructor calls below.
@Rise: a marker annotation from com.alan.clients.api tagging this class as part of the Rise client's module set. It is processed at startup when the client scans and registers modules.

@ModuleInfo declares the module: a translation-component key for the name (module.combat.disabler.name, a leftover from when the module sat in combat, hence the combat path) and for the description (module.exploit.disabler.description), with category = Category.EXPLOIT. Rise resolves the language keys at runtime from its locale files.
Class declaration: Disabler extends Module, the client's base module class. Every Rise module follows this shape; the instance fields below are the entire body.

cubecraft toggle: a BooleanValue named 'Cubecraft', off by default, bound to a CubeCraftDisabler component instance. The fourth constructor argument is the component that runs while the value is enabled.

mineLandKick toggle: 'Mine Land Kick Checks' bound to MineLandKickDisabler. Named after the Mine Land server's kick checks, which the component desynchronizes so the server stops disconnecting the player.
verus toggle: 'Verus Checks' bound to VerusCustomDisabler, the bypass suite for the Verus anticheat.
vehicle toggle: 'Vehicle Packets' bound to VehicleDisabler, a component that handles the serverbound stream while the player is mounted.
teleport toggle: 'Force Server Teleport' bound to TeleportDisabler, which pushes the server into confirming teleports so the client keeps a consistent position.
vulcan toggle: 'Vulcan Checks' bound to VulcanDisabler, the bypass set for the Vulcan anticheat.
sprint toggle: 'Cancel Sprint Packet' bound to SprintDisabler, which stops C0BPacketEntityAction sprint-state packets from reaching the server.
omnisprint toggle: 'OmniSprint' bound to OmniSprintDisabler, a variant that lets the client sprint in every direction (including backwards) without the server-side sprint flags.

universocraft toggle: bound to UniversoCraftDisabler, the state machine aimed at the UniversoCraft network. The component tracks S07PacketRespawn and C02PacketUseEntity to time its transaction corruption.
riseBalance toggle: 'Rise Balance Timer Abuse' bound to RiseBalanceDisabler, a timer exploit tuned against Rise's own balance anticheat.
cancelTransactions toggle: 'Cancel Transactions' bound to TransactionDisabler, which eats C0FPacketConfirmTransaction confirmations to break the server's inventory-transaction tracking.
Abilities toggle: bound to AbilitiesDisabler, which spoofs C13PacketPlayerAbilities. The field name breaks the lowercase convention (a capital A in Abilities), a minor naming inconsistency.
input toggle: 'Input' bound to InputDisabler, which handles the C07PacketPlayerDigging / C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement stream to desynchronize server-side input validation.
spectate toggle: 'Spectate' bound to SpectateDisabler, which injects C18PacketSpectate for the player's own entity to desync the server's camera tracking.
cancelKeepAlives toggle: 'Cancel Keep Alive' bound to KeepAliveDisabler, which cancels C00PacketKeepAlive packets outright (no echo, unlike a ping-spoof).
deprecated toggle: a plain BooleanValue with no component. It is the master switch for the legacy section; the constructor wires every later value's visibility to it.

hypixelSlime toggle: 'Hypixel Slime (Deprecated)' reuses the AbilitiesDisabler component from line 48, so enabling it behaves identically to Abilities. Kept for users who still remember the old Hypixel slime bypass by name.
mmcReachPartial toggle: 'MMC Partial Reach (Deprecated)' reuses TransactionDisabler, the same component as Cancel Transactions.
mmcKeepSprint toggle: 'MMC Keep Sprint (Deprecated)' reuses SprintDisabler, the same component as Cancel Sprint Packet.
dynamicPVP toggle: 'Dynamic PVP (Deprecated)' bound to DynamicPVPDisabler, a standalone legacy component for the old Dynamic PVP bypass.
ghostly toggle: 'Ghostly (Deprecated)' bound to GhostlyDisabler, a standalone legacy component.
lunar toggle: 'Lunar (Deprecated)' bound to LunarDisabler, a standalone legacy component aimed at the Lunar client anticheat.
Constructor. Empty parameter list; the module is self-registering through @ModuleInfo, so no registration calls are needed here.
Local lookahead flag: starts false and is set to true once the constructor has passed the Deprecated toggle. It drives the hideIf wiring in the loop below.
Walks every value the module declares (getValues() returns the fields in declaration order). The loop assigns hideIf to each value based on the flag from the previous iteration.

For every value declared after the Deprecated toggle, hideIf = () -> !this.deprecated.getValue() hides it from the settings UI unless the Deprecated master switch is enabled. The lambda captures the module's deprecated value, so toggling it live re-shows the legacy section.

Sets the lookahead flag when the current value's name equals 'deprecated' (case-insensitive). Because the flag is read before the assignment on each pass, the Deprecated toggle itself is never hidden.
